title: STRANGE MINUTE #24

lines.text: Scientists just found Betelgeuse's secret twin.
lines.say: Scientists just found Beetle-juice's secret twin.

lines.text: Betelgeuse is the red shoulder of Orion. You can see it tonight.
lines.say: Beetle-juice is the red shoulder of Orion. You can see it tonight.

lines.text: It's huge: about 700 times wider than our Sun.
lines.say: It's huge: about seven hundred times wider than our Sun.

lines.text: Put it where the Sun is, and it would swallow Mercury, Venus, Earth and Mars.
For a century, astronomers wondered why it dims in a strange six-year rhythm.
Now they've seen the culprit: a companion star named Siwarha.
lines.say: Now they've seen the culprit: a companion star named Si-war-ha.

lines.text: In Arabic, that means her bracelet.
It's about one and a half times the mass of our Sun.
And it orbits so close, it plows through Betelgeuse's outer atmosphere.
lines.say: And it orbits so close, it plows through Beetle-juice's outer atmosphere.

lines.text: One lap every six years, leaving a wake like a speedboat.
But its orbit is shrinking. They could merge within 9,000 years.
lines.say: But its orbit is shrinking. They could merge within nine thousand years.

lines.text: Unless Betelgeuse explodes first, so bright you could see it in daylight.
lines.say: Unless Beetle-juice explodes first, so bright you could see it in daylight.

lines.text: So which happens first? Drop your guess.

sources: 2025–2026 Gemini/Hubble results: companion Siwarha (IAU-approved name Sept 2025, 'her bracelet'), ~1.5 solar masses, ~6-yr orbit at ~4 AU through Betelgeuse's outer atmosphere, leaves a wake
NASA via Live Science: Betelgeuse ~700× the Sun's diameter (radius ~3.3 AU → past Mars, into the asteroid belt); ~650 light-years
A Betelgeuse supernova is expected to be visible in daylight
